channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Consumer Protection Committee Receives Frequent Complaints on Specific Issues
item.description: The Consumer Rights Protection Committee has revealed the most common complaints received from citizens. The specific nature of these complaints indicates recurring issues within consumer services and product quality. Further details on the types of complaints and the committee's response are expected.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Second Phase of 'Umai' Mortgage Program for Women
item.description: Kazakhstan begins the second phase of the 'Umai' mortgage program for women on November 3rd. The Asian Development Bank has allocated 20 billion tenge to Family Bank as a second tranche to widely implement the program among Kazakh women. The program offers a low initial down payment, making homeownership accessible.

item.title: Alatau City Bank Becomes First Second-Tier Bank on KASE Digital Assets Market
item.description: Alatau City Bank has become the first second-tier bank in Kazakhstan to join the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange's (KASE) digital financial assets (CFA) platform. This move aims to develop digital financial instruments for businesses, expand corporate client opportunities, and create new products using tokenized real-world assets (RWA).

item.title: Kazakhstan Focuses on Infrastructure Development for Agricultural and Economic Growth
item.description: Kazakhstan is prioritizing infrastructure development, including roads and water supply, to boost agricultural productivity and create jobs. The government plans to increase funding for agricultural financing and support the development of processing and storage facilities. This initiative aims to ensure that economic growth benefits all households.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans 23.2% Budget Revenue Increase by 2027
item.description: Tajikistan's government plans to increase state budget revenues to 80.1 billion somoni by 2027, a 23.2% rise from 2026. The budget proposal, discussed by President Emomali Rahmon, allocates 36.7 billion somoni to the social sector. Future projections indicate continued revenue growth through 2029.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Fines Up to 9.4 Million Tenge for Unauthorized Water Use
item.description: Kazakhstan is considering fines ranging from 235,000 to 9.4 million tenge for drawing water from irrigation canals without a contract. Proposed amendments to the Water Code would allow inspectors to check for violations without prior registration. These measures aim to address unauthorized water consumption from main and inter-farm canals.

item.title: Kazakhstan Declares 2027 Year of Public Construction, Prioritizing Infrastructure Modernization
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced 2027 as the 'Year of Public Construction' in Kazakhstan, emphasizing comprehensive infrastructure modernization. This initiative, termed 'People's Construction,' aims to build a technologically advanced, competitive economy with high living standards for future generations. The government will develop an unprecedented infrastructure modernization plan.

item.title: Yemen's Houthi rebels launch new attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure
item.description: Yemen's Houthi movement, Ansar Allah, claimed responsibility for new attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities, airports, and military targets. The group stated that ballistic missiles and drones were used, hitting a refinery in Ras Tanura and Saudi Aramco facilities in Abqaiq and Rabigh. The Riyadh airport was also targeted. Oil prices rose amid the escalation.

item.title: President Tokayev Outlines National Priorities in Traditional Address to the People
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has outlined the nation's key priorities and development directions for a new historical period in his traditional address to the people. He emphasized the principle of 'Law and Order,' the importance of updating the Civil Code, and declared 2027 the 'Year of Nationwide Construction'.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Implement President's Address on Key Tasks for New Historical Period
item.description: Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov chaired a government meeting to discuss measures for implementing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address. The address outlines goals for a just, strong, clean, and advanced Kazakhstan, emphasizing the need to leverage the nation's potential and modern opportunities. The 'People's Construction' program aims to drive infrastructure reforms, boost employment, and improve citizen welfare.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Meets with Leaders of Leading Turkish Companies
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting with executives from prominent Turkish companies, including Evyap Holding, OYAK, EKSIM Holding, and Anadolu Group. Discussions focused on various investment projects. The meeting aimed to strengthen economic ties and explore new avenues for collaboration between Uzbekistan and Turkey.

item.title: Shymkent Court Overturns 12-Year Sentence for Former Security Official
item.description: A Shymkent court has overturned a 12-year prison sentence for Manat Sarbasov, former deputy head of the National Security Committee's department. The cassation court found violations of legal procedures during the initial trial. Sarbasov, previously convicted of bribery and other charges, remains in custody as the case will be retried by a different panel of judges.

item.title: Head of People's Council Outlines Key Tasks for Implementing President's Address
item.description: Yerlan Koshanov chaired an expanded meeting of the Presidium of the People's Council of Kazakhstan, focusing on implementing the President's address "Urgent Tasks of Kazakhstan in a New Historical Era." Koshanov emphasized the address's strategic importance and the need for active participation and accountability from council members to achieve national goals.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Electricity Consumption Rises Nearly 30 Percent Annually
item.description: Electricity consumption in Kyrgyzstan has significantly increased, with daily usage up by 29.1 percent compared to the same period last year, according to the National Electric Network of Kyrgyzstan. The republic's current daily consumption stands at 66.022 million kilowatt-hours. The company urges citizens to use electricity rationally and conserve resources.

item.title: Iran Imports $2 Billion in Military Equipment Bypassing US Blockade
item.description: Iran has imported $2 billion worth of military equipment, circumventing US sanctions and blockade. According to a Reuters investigation, Iran established a network of approximately 5,000 special companies since January 2025 to facilitate this import. These companies, often starting with 'MOD' and linked to the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, are registered at the Ministry of Defense's address.

item.title: Russian Forces Strike Dnipro Railway Station with Drones, Killing at Least 14
item.description: Russian forces attacked the Dnipro railway station with drones on October 29, resulting in at least 14 deaths and 13 injuries, four critically. Ukraine's railway company reported the drone hit a platform where a train was stopped. Russia frequently targets Ukrainian railway infrastructure.

item.title: Dozens of Drug Packages Seized from Driver in Almaty
item.description: Police in Almaty detained a driver under the influence of drugs and discovered his Toyota Camry filled with marijuana. The man claimed the drugs were for personal use. Authorities found 23 containers and seven bags of the substance in the car.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Regional Technological Development Platform at Innovation Forum
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed the creation of a regional technological development platform to strengthen Central Asian ties at the InnoWeek.Uz — 2026 innovation forum in Tashkent. The strategy, presented by Kyrgyzstan's Minister of Science, Higher Education, and Innovation, aims to establish a unified educational and research space for Turkic countries. Key proposals include student business incubators and joint high-tech research.

item.title: Cryptocurrency Exchange Binance Freezes Operations Amid Suspected Major Hack
item.description: The cryptocurrency exchange Binance has suspended all deposit and withdrawal operations following a suspected large-scale hack. Billions of dollars were reportedly moved from the platform within hours. Binance has frozen assets worth $2.5 billion as part of an investigation into the incident, with former CEO Changpeng Zhao confirming the likely attack.

item.title: UN Reports 325% Surge in Afghan Opium Cultivation by 2026 Despite Taliban Ban
item.description: Opium cultivation in Afghanistan has surged by 325% by 2026, according to the UN, exceeding 43,000 hectares despite the Taliban's ban. Opium production reached 1,466 tons, a significant increase from 296 tons last year. This rise indicates challenges in enforcing drug control policies in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Proposes Introducing a Luxury Tax
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has proposed the introduction of a luxury tax. He announced this during his address to the nation. Tokayev did not specify the wealth threshold for this tax, asking the government and parliament to study the issue and make proposals.

item.title: Kazakhstani Surrogates Face Exploitation and Health Risks Abroad
item.description: Georgian surrogacy centers are attracting women from Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, promising financial benefits. However, many surrogates face health complications, loss of payments, and abandonment with their problems. A 36-year-old woman shared her experience of undergoing surrogacy to fund her children's education, only to face unforeseen difficulties.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Head of Anadolu Group Holding in Ankara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Kamilhan Suleyman Yazici, Chairman of the Board of Directors of Anadolu Group Holding, in Ankara. The meeting highlighted the company's significant investments in Uzbekistan's beverage and automotive sectors as a testament to their confidence in the country's reforms. Discussions included further investment projects for SamAuto modernization, capacity expansion, and export growth, as well as potential retail network entry and agricultural projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Discuss Cooperation in Energy, Mining, and Infrastructure
item.description: During the Turkic States summit, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Ebubekir Tivnikli, Chairman of EKSIM Holding. They discussed expanding cooperation in renewable energy, geology, mining, infrastructure, electric vehicle charging stations, and the food industry. Discussions also covered building new power lines and implementing geological projects in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets with Head of Turkish Company OYAK
item.description: During the OTS summit, Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Murat Yalçıntaş, CEO of Turkey's OYAK company. The Turkish partner expressed interest in joint investment projects in chemical industry, geology, and construction in Uzbekistan, and in participating in the construction of residential complexes in New Tashkent.

item.title: Turkmenistan Meets IMF After Report on Missing Data
item.description: Turkmen officials met with an International Monetary Fund representative in Ashgabat. This follows an IMF conclusion that Turkmenistan breached its obligations by failing to provide key data, including information on international reserve assets and balance of payments. The ministry stated discussions focused on cooperation prospects.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Turkey Sign Agreements to Boost Business and Trade
item.description: Following high-level talks in Ankara, Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev and Turkey's President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan signed an agreement to establish a High-Level Council for Business Support. A package of bilateral documents was also signed, including protocols to expand preferential trade and enhance information exchange on goods and vehicles crossing borders.

item.title: Uzbek President Meets Turkish President to Strengthen Strategic Partnership
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev held a meeting with the Turkish President to discuss strengthening strategic partnership relations between the two countries. Key areas of focus included political-diplomatic, trade-economic, and cultural-humanitarian cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Entrepreneurship Support and Private Property Protection
item.description: Uzbekistan's state policy prioritizes supporting small businesses and protecting private property rights. The Business Ombudsman's office in the Fergana region has taken measures against 101 officials for violating entrepreneurs' rights, imposing fines. Additionally, 20 submissions, 30 conclusions, and 49 warnings were issued to state bodies to ensure legal compliance and address violations.

item.title: Uzbek President Inaugurates Turkic Civilization Garden in Ankara
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev participated in a cultural program at the Turkic States Organization (OTS) summit in Ankara. He, along with other leaders and their spouses, inaugurated the Turkic Civilization Garden, showcasing traditional yurts, applied arts, and achievements of Turkic peoples. The leaders also visited the Malazgirt center and planted oak saplings.

item.title: Taliban Member Kills Two, Injures Three in Badakhshan Province Shooting
item.description: A Taliban member reportedly opened fire in the Argo district of Badakhshan province, killing two people and injuring three others. The incident occurred three nights prior in the village of Ghozak Dara. The alleged shooter, identified as a Taliban member, was arrested following the event.

item.title: Turkmenistan President Begins Working Visit to Turkey for Summit
item.description: President Serdar Berdimuhamedow of Turkmenistan has departed on a working visit to the Republic of Turkey to attend the 13th Summit of the Turkic States. The visit aims to further strengthen Turkmen-Turkish relations, which are based on shared history and cultural values. The summit is expected to enhance regional cooperation in energy, transport, and logistics.

item.title: Uzbek-Turkish cooperation reaches new heights in tourism sector
item.description: Tourism between Uzbekistan and Turkey has seen dynamic growth, with bilateral agreements and increased tourist exchanges. The number of Turkish tourists to Uzbekistan nearly doubled in two years, reaching 149,146 in 2024. Uzbekistan also saw a 17.4% increase in its citizens visiting Turkey in 2025. This success aligns with Uzbekistan's overall tourism boom, positioning it among states with high international tourism growth rates.

item.title: UN Rapporteur Warns Against Granting Legitimacy to Taliban Without Rights Improvements
item.description: UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett cautioned that international engagement with the Taliban should not legitimize their rule without verifiable improvements in human rights. He noted that repression and discrimination in Afghanistan have become increasingly entrenched since the Taliban's return to power five years ago.

item.title: Poor Air Quality Expected in Almaty and Four Other Kazakh Cities on October 30
item.description: Kazakhstan's 'Kazgidromet' forecasts unfavorable meteorological conditions for air quality in five cities on October 30, including Almaty, Aktobe, Atyrau, and Shymkent. Astana will experience these conditions at night. Unfavorable conditions arise from calm winds, fog, and temperature inversions, leading to pollutant accumulation. Residents are advised to limit outdoor exposure, especially near roads, and vulnerable groups should take precautions.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans to Phase Out Cash Payments on Electric Trains and Buses by 2030
item.description: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Transport has drafted a presidential resolution to gradually transition to cashless payments for passenger transport. The plan aims to eliminate cash transactions on suburban trains and intercity buses by January 1, 2030, with all payments made electronically. To encourage adoption, a temporary discount on electronic tickets is proposed for passengers.

item.title: Kazakh Citizen Sentenced in Russia for Illegal Immigrant Smuggling
item.description: A 43-year-old citizen of Kazakhstan, employed as a train driver by Russian Railways, has been sentenced to two years and five months in prison in Omsk, Russia. He was found guilty of organizing the illegal entry of a foreign national into the Russian Federation as part of a group. The court heard that he facilitated the border crossing for a fee of 100,000 rubles.

item.title: Kazakhstan Issues Storm Warning for October 30: Freezing Temperatures, Snow, and Ice Expected
item.description: A storm warning has been issued for October 30 across 16 regions of Kazakhstan, with forecasts of rain, snow, ice, fog, and wind gusts up to 20 m/s. Freezing temperatures are expected in the south and southeast. Specific regions like Pavlodar, East Kazakhstan, Abai, and North Kazakhstan will experience mixed precipitation and icy conditions. Jetisu and Almaty regions anticipate night frosts, with temperatures dropping significantly in mountainous areas.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Unified Digital Transport Platform for Seamless Travel
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to launch a unified national digital transport platform, "Bir yo‘l," by January 1, 2028. This platform will integrate rail, air, bus, and urban transport systems, allowing passengers to plan journeys door-to-door, book tickets, and make payments through a single system. The initiative aims to simplify travel and enhance passenger experience.

item.title: Central Asian Cultural Figures Honored with State Awards
item.description: Vice President Yerlan Karin presented state awards to prominent cultural and art figures from Central Asian countries in Akorda. The awards, including the 'Dostyk' Order of the II degree, recognized contributions to strengthening friendship and developing cultural ties.
